title: Real-tmux bridge tests fail under apicover-enforce's package-parallel run: the sandboxed fake REPL misses its boot budget (2 occurrences)
summary: On 2026-09-30 the local `make -C go apicover-enforce` (go test -count=1 -tags integration -coverprofile over every enforced package at once) failed twice on internal/bridge real-tmux tests: TestRealTmuxSandboxTerminalConfinement (train #731's floor), then TestRealTmuxSandboxTerminalConfinement, TestRealTmux_BracketedMultilinePromptPreservesBytes, TestRealTmux_E2E_LiveInjection_UnblocksAgent and TestRealTmux_HappyPath (PR #732's floor), each 'REPL prompt never appeared' then exit 80. Both times the package passed alone under the same invocation (42.7s), passed in the same floor's test-integration, and the diffs never touched internal/bridge; CI's go jobs were green. The first run overlapped another heavy suite on the host; the second ran alone, so the package-parallel coverage run itself supplies enough load.
fix: Make the boot wait of the real-tmux fixtures load-aware (derive it from a measured boot of the fake REPL, or run these tests serially under a shared lock like the integration tier's retake), so a slow host yields a slow pass, never a false red; the local floor mirror must not go red where CI is green.
acceptance: `make -C go apicover-enforce` passes on a quiet host three runs in a row (red today, intermittently)
The real-tmux fixtures' boot budget is derived, not a fixed wall-clock constant
